text:
sam: noticed our eu-west GPU pool at 100% alloc around 09:12 UTC, but prometheus shows very low sustained token throughput. looks like weird short-lived pods flooding the scheduler.
mei: can you paste the pod list? suspecting many tiny jobs from research sweeps.
sam: here — `kubectl get pods -n research -o wide | grep gpu | awk '{print $1, $3, $5, $6}' | head -n 20` -> lots of jobs with runtime 1-3m, QOS BestEffort, requests: gpu:1, cpu:100m.
leo: ugh BestEffort + gpu request is the worst. autoscaler sees many pending pods then they finish quickly so scaler overshoots. this matches a "heartbeat" style scaling misread.
anya: infra-bot triggered provision of 6 new nodes in nodepool-gpu-eu-spot at 09:14, most got REGISTERED then drained within minutes.
infra-bot: [automated] Detected rapid scale-up events (3 events in 120s). Suggested action: enable scale-up stabilization or apply podGroup throttles.
mei: immediate mitigation: cordon nodepool-gpu-eu-spot nodes that are <5m old to stop churn? we should avoid killing running inference.
leo: doing a soft stop: `kubectl label node <node> no-autoscale=true` for the newest 3 nodes, then scale the nodepool down stabilization window to 300s in CA config.
sam: applied label to nodes: ip-10-0-12-34, ip-10-0-14-99, ip-10-0-15-22.
anya: also throttling the research cron temporarily. `kubectl scale cronjob/param-sweep -n research --replicas=1` -> changed to hourly.
oncall: set pager muted for non-critical alerts for 10m while we stabilize.
leo: root cause hypothesis: many small experiment jobs were updated to request GPU without proper Queue/Backoff; scheduler and CA react to pending spikes causing a feedback loop.
mei: proposed longer term: (1) add a small admission controller that groups short-lived GPU tasks into a queue, (2) set PodDisruptionBudget + PodPriority for production jobs, (3) update autoscaler to use pending pod age threshold before scaling up.
sam: also consider a circuit-breaker on nodepool provisioning: block scale-ups for X minutes after >N churns.
anya: creating a quick RFC ticket for circuit-breaker and short job admission: https://redwood/boards/infra/GPUSurgeCircuit-125 (placeholder).
deploy-bot: [deploy] patch applied to cluster-autoscaler config: scaleUpDelay: 240s, maxNodeProvisionRepeat: 3.
leo: after changes, new events show scale-ups suppressed and many small pods start queuing. node utilization drops from 98% to 65% over 6m.
mei: final step: reach out to research team to mark their low-latency sweeps as queueable workloads; emailed @research-leads.
sam: monitoring: keeping an eye for 30m, will uncordon nodes if any legitimate prod eviction. thanks all. :thumbsup:
anya: postmortem follow-ups: update docs, add scheduling quota limits for research, and add a dashboard showing short-job churn metric.
infra-bot: [automated] Incident closed for now (mitigated). Remember to file a postmortem within 48h.
